skills.plan_reason: Generated frames must remain technically clean enough to judge the pendulum apparatus, protractor markings, rest marker, string, bob, and fixed measurement setup.
The rollout should show present, temporally smooth pendulum motion after release from the marked angle, without jitter, teleporting, or discontinuous bob/string movement.
The pivot, string, protractor, rest marker, bob, and surrounding apparatus should keep stable identity, geometry, scale, and material appearance across frames.
The bob should respond plausibly to release with gravity-driven swinging and damping, while the apparatus and camera remain fixed.

causal_checks: After release, gravity accelerates the bob downward toward the vertical centerline.
The bob speed is greatest near the lowest point of the swing.
The bob slows as it climbs away from the lowest point on the opposite side.
With no push, the bob does not swing higher than the release angle except for negligible visual error.
The string remains taut and the bob follows an arc about the fixed pivot.
The pivot and measurement board do not translate or rotate while the bob moves.
Successive peaks occur on alternating sides of the vertical.
Any amplitude loss is gradual rather than an abrupt stop or reversal.
controlled_variables: measurement camera position, angle, focal length, and framing remain fixed
pivot, support frame, board, protractor, marked angle indicator, and apparatus anchors remain fixed
bob mass and shape remain constant
release angle corresponds to the marked medium level 3 position
bob is released from rest with zero initial tangential velocity
no external contact or drive is applied after release

expected_response.amplitude: The first opposite-side peak should be approximately comparable to the release angle, with any damping causing only gradual reduction over successive swings.
expected_response.energy_behavior: Gravitational potential energy converts to kinetic energy on the downswing and back to potential energy on the upswing, with no sudden gain in amplitude because no push is applied.
expected_response.motion: The bob begins moving from the marked off-vertical angle toward the lowest point under gravity, passes through the vertical with maximum speed, rises to the opposite side, slows near its turning point, and repeats as a pendular oscillation.
expected_response.period: The oscillation period should remain approximately consistent from swing to swing for the same string length.
expected_response.trajectory: The bob follows a smooth circular arc centered on the fixed pivot, constrained by the taut string.

failure_modes: bob receives an obvious push or starts with nonzero tangential velocity
bob falls, detaches, or moves in a straight line instead of an arc
string stretches, slackens, changes length, or disconnects
pivot or support frame moves during the swing
camera pans, zooms, cuts, or changes perspective
protractor, board, label, or marked angle shifts position
bob swings to an amplitude much larger than the release angle without cause
bob stops abruptly without collision or damping explanation
motion is chaotic, non-periodic, or inconsistent with gravity-driven pendulum oscillation
expected_spec.intervention: Set the release condition to medium level 3 and release the pendulum bob from the marked angular displacement with no added push or impulse.
protected_anchors: bob attached to the string throughout
expected_spec.target_system: Simple pendulum bob suspended from a fixed pivot over a measurement board with a protractor and marked release angle.
